Which US states have no state income tax, and does that affect my monthly budget?

Nine states currently charge no state income tax: Alaska, Florida, Nevada, New Hampshire, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Washington, and Wyoming. Living in one of these can raise take-home pay by roughly 4–9% of gross income compared to California or New York, but several of these states offset the difference with higher sales tax or property tax — compare the full tax picture (income + sales + property), not just the income tax line, before assuming a no-income-tax state is automatically cheaper overall.
